newsitem.title: USA: NACo panel tells Congress delay internet tax bill.
newsitem.headline: NACo panel tells Congress delay internet tax bill.

text.p: National Association of Counties' board of directors this weekend urged the U.S. Congress to delay enacting Internet taxation legislation until its potential impact on localities is carefully studied.

The board, meeting in Baltimore this week for the group's 62nd annual conference, adopted a two-page resolution on the issue at a session Sunday. The 3,400 delegates attending the conference are expected to adopt the draft resolution Tuesday.

The board wants a freeze on congressional action on identical House and Senate bills that call for a national moratorium on state and local taxes that target the Internet, such as taxes on Internet access or online services.
The draft resolution says NACo opposes any unlimited moratorium on state and local government taxation of electronic commerce.

It urges the bills' delay until a "thorough and impartial study of the nature of electronic commerce and the effect of such commerce upon ... state and local governments and their taxpayers is completed."

NACo's board warned that states and localities derive substantial revenues for public safety, water and wastewater operations and other functions from sales, property and other revenues from telecommunications providers.
